summary.text: 书 is the standardized simplified form of 書. The traditional graph is analyzed as a writing-related compound, while the simplified shape comes from regularizing a cursive form and no longer shows that analysis clearly.

formation.text: The traditional graph 書 is analyzed as phonosemantic: 聿 contributes the writing-related meaning and 者 is the phonetic element. The modern 书 is its standardized simplified counterpart, formed by regularizing a cursive shape.

components.text: Within 書, 聿 is the semantic element associated with a writing brush and writing. The evidence also gives it a historical comparison glossed as “writing stylus or brush,” but does not establish the object’s original pictorial form.
Within 書, 者 is identified as the phonetic element. The traditional analysis supports that role; the sound comparison is clearer in the supplied historical reconstructions than in modern Mandarin.

sound.text: The supplied Baxter–Sagart comparisons are 書 MC syo, OC *s-ta and 者 MC tsyaeX, OC *tAʔ. The Old Chinese forms share an initial *t and a related rhyme, supporting the traditional phonetic analysis; modern Mandarin shū and zhě differ more noticeably.
sound.system: Mandarin; Baxter–Sagart 2014 Middle Chinese and Old Chinese

history.text: 書 is traditionally analyzed as built from 聿 and 者, with the latter supplying sound. The modern simplified form 书 regularizes a cursive form of 書; this is a change in the written graph, not evidence that its original construction was a hand holding a brush.
Seal-style and bronze-style redraws are identified in the cited material, but they are not independently dated specimens. They do not establish a sequence of graphic development.

uncertainties.text: The earliest securely dated attestation of 書 and a dated sequence of its historical forms remain unresolved in the cited accounts.

senses.text: The traditional gloss associates 書 with writing or setting something down. The cited account does not identify this as the earliest attested use.
書 is also used to mean “record.” The cited example does not establish when this use arose relative to the other senses.
The character is used for writing or text; the cited examples do not date this sense in relation to the others.
“Book” is a current meaning of the character, also found in cited classical examples. The available evidence does not date its development from “write” or “text.”
The character also means “letter” or “document.” The cited examples do not establish when these uses arose or how they relate chronologically to the others.

limitations.text: The cited examples attest several uses, but do not establish a chronological path among writing, recording, text, book, letter and document.

overview.text: 书 is the simplified form of 書, traditionally analyzed as a writing-related compound: 聿 contributes the writing meaning, while 者 supplies a sound element. The simplified graph comes from regularizing a cursive form.

components.text: In 書, 聿 is the writing-related element.
In 書, 者 is the sound element; older sound comparisons help explain the relationship.

relationships.text: 书 is the standardized simplified form of 書, described as regularizing a cursive form into standard script.
In the traditional analysis of 書, 聿 contributes the writing-related meaning.
The traditional analysis assigns 者 the phonetic role in 書. The supplied Baxter–Sagart comparisons show a closer historical sound correspondence than modern Mandarin readings do.
